reasons: Declarations cannot prove the server sends matching data.
Many optional fields mean callers must check for them, and that is not visible here.
No test in the packet checks the server data against these shapes.

terms.meaning: a written description of what a value must contain, checked before the app runs
a named type that lists the fields a record must have
a field that may be missing, marked with a question mark
the record of where a value came from and why it was chosen

sections.name: Confidence
sections.title: Confidence levels
sections.what: Lists the three confidence labels used in the app: high, medium and low.
sections.why: Keeps confidence labels to a fixed set.
sections.watch_out: Numeric confidence scores elsewhere are separate and are not these labels.

sections.name: ProvenanceKind
sections.title: Ways a value can be obtained
sections.what: Lists how a value was found: measured, from the source, inferred, typical, rule based, staggered rule, or abstract.
sections.why: Lets the screen tell the viewer how much to trust each value.
sections.watch_out: Any new kind must be handled wherever these kinds are displayed.

sections.name: Phase
sections.title: Construction phase categories
sections.what: Lists the construction work types, such as foundations, steel, piping, testing and commissioning, plus milestone and unknown.
sections.why: Lets each activity be grouped and coloured by type of work.
sections.watch_out: The unknown value is the fallback. A new phase must also be mapped in the lifecycle file, or it lands in the unclassified group.

sections.name: StructureClass
sections.title: Broad structure types
sections.what: Lists the broad physical kinds of structure, such as below ground, concrete, steel frame, process block, or open area.
sections.why: Used to choose how a structure is drawn and grouped.
sections.watch_out: Adding a type requires the drawing code to handle it, or the structure may not appear as expected.

sections.name: Vector3
sections.title: Three-number position or size
sections.what: Holds three numbers, one each for the x, y and z directions.
sections.why: Used for positions, sizes and rotations throughout the model.
sections.watch_out: The units are not stated in this declaration.

sections.name: Provenance
sections.title: Record of where a value came from
sections.what: Holds the kind of origin, a reason, and optional source file and page or area references.
sections.why: So every shown value can be traced to its origin.
sections.watch_out: The source and range fields can be empty, so the display must handle missing references.

sections.name: GeometryPlan
sections.title: Planned 3D shape of a component
sections.what: Describes the basic shape, its position, size, rotation, how it is revealed on the timeline, and a detail budget.
sections.why: Gives the 3D view what it needs to draw one component.
sections.watch_out: The triangle budget caps the drawing detail, so changing it changes how smooth the shape looks.

sections.name: AssemblyPartRecipe
sections.title: Repeatable part of an assembly
sections.what: Describes one part of a reusable assembly, with its position within the assembly, its size, its material and how many copies to place.
sections.why: Lets one template produce many identical parts.
sections.watch_out: A repeat count of one means a single copy, so code must not assume copies exist.

sections.name: ParametricPart
sections.title: Detailed part linked to source facts
sections.what: Describes a sub part whose size and position are traced back to source facts, with a record of where each measurement came from.
sections.why: Lets the viewer see why each dimension was chosen.
sections.watch_out: Many fields are optional or lists that may be empty, so the code must not assume they exist.

sections.name: ComponentSchedule
sections.title: Dates for one component
sections.what: Lists the planned, actual, baseline and forecast start and finish texts for one component, plus the data date.
sections.why: Gives each component the dates it needs for every date set.
sections.watch_out: The dates are stored as text, so they must be read before they can be compared.

sections.name: ModelComponent
sections.title: One component in the model
sections.what: Describes a single 3D element with its name, location, class, quantity, schedule, shape, confidence and evidence list.
sections.why: This is the main unit the 3D view and the checklists work with.
sections.watch_out: Many fields are optional, so callers must handle missing values.

sections.name: TruthState
sections.title: How well a fact is supported
sections.what: Lists support levels for a fact, from corroborated and source stated, down through derived, inferred, typical and rule, to conflicted and unsupported.
sections.why: Lets the viewer see how much a value can be relied on.
sections.watch_out: Conflicted means sources disagree. It is not a fault in the app.

sections.name: EvidenceRecord
sections.title: One piece of source evidence
sections.what: Describes one fact taken from a source file, with its value, unit, file, page, extraction method, confidence, and review status.
sections.why: Makes each value auditable back to the original document.
sections.watch_out: Many fields are free text, so they are not checked against a fixed list.

sections.name: ActivityComponentMapping
sections.title: Link between an activity and a component
sections.what: Records that a schedule activity changes a particular component, with the quantity, the reveal rule and the confidence.
sections.why: Lets the 3D view reveal a component when its activity happens.
sections.watch_out: The reveal rule text decides when the component appears, so a wrong rule shows the component at the wrong time.

sections.name: ActivityStory
sections.title: Plain-language story for an activity
sections.what: Describes one activity with its name, phase, dates on every date set, linked components, and explanations for three audiences.
sections.why: Lets the viewer read what is happening, written for beginners or for professionals.
sections.watch_out: The explanation text is shown as written, so it must be kept accurate and in the right audience.

sections.name: Playlist
sections.title: Named list for guided viewing
sections.what: Describes a named list of stories or components that the viewer can step through.
sections.why: Supports guided tours of the project.
sections.watch_out: The component list is optional, so code must handle its absence.

sections.name: SitePlanExtent
sections.title: Site size
sections.what: Holds the width and depth of the site, its unit, its sources and its limits.
sections.why: Used to draw the site area in the 3D scene.
sections.watch_out: The unit is text, so check it before drawing, or the site may be sized wrongly.

sections.name: ProgrammeProject
sections.title: One project in a programme
sections.what: Describes one project in a multi-project programme, with its activity count, dates, detail level and position in the overall layout.
sections.why: Lets the programme view place each project.
sections.watch_out: The fidelity value says whether document detail exists. Schedule-only projects have less detail.

sections.name: ProgrammeActivity
sections.title: One activity in a programme
sections.what: Describes one activity within a programme, with its dates on every date set and its evidence reference.
sections.why: Lets the programme view list and date each activity.
sections.watch_out: Each date can be missing, so every date needs a check.

sections.name: ProgrammeRelationship
sections.title: Link between two programme activities
sections.what: Describes a dependency from one activity to another, possibly across projects, with an optional type and lag in hours.
sections.why: Lets the programme view show how work depends on other work.
sections.watch_out: The relation type and lag can be empty, so treat missing values as unknown.

sections.name: ProgrammeModel
sections.title: Whole programme response
sections.what: Describes the full programme data returned by the server, with lists of projects, activities, links, evidence and paging counts.
sections.why: Lets the programme view page through large schedules.
sections.watch_out: The totals and offsets control paging, so a partial result is possible. The limitations list should be shown to the viewer.

sections.name: StructureRecord
sections.title: Grouped structure record
sections.what: Describes one grouped structure, with its classification scores, dates, activity counts, neighbours and layout reason.
sections.why: Lets the app place and explain each structure in the layout.
sections.watch_out: The scores come from a classifier with no fixed range stated here, so do not compare them as percentages.

sections.name: TimelineLaneItem
sections.title: Abstract activity on the timeline
sections.what: Describes an activity that has no 3D shape but still appears on the timeline, with its dates on every date set.
sections.why: Lets non-physical work show on the timeline.
sections.watch_out: Its materiality is always abstract, so code must not expect a shape for it.

sections.name: DateBasisBounds
sections.title: Start and finish for one date set
sections.what: Holds an optional start text and an optional finish text for one date set.
sections.why: Used to declare the overall range for each date set.
sections.watch_out: Both values can be missing, so check them before use.

sections.name: TimelineLanePage
sections.title: One page of timeline items
sections.what: Holds a list of timeline items together with the total number and the paging offset and limit.
sections.why: Lets large lane lists load in pages.
sections.watch_out: The total can be larger than the number of items shown, so do not treat the list as complete.

sections.name: TimelineAdjacentEvent
sections.title: Next or previous event time
sections.what: Holds the timestamp text of the next or previous event, or nothing if there is none.
sections.why: Used when stepping through the timeline.
sections.watch_out: Nothing means there is no further event, so the caller must handle it.

sections.name: GroupingCandidate
sections.title: One way of grouping activities
sections.what: Holds the scores and counts for one candidate grouping method, and whether it was the one selected.
sections.why: Lets the viewer compare grouping methods and see why one was chosen.
sections.watch_out: Reason for the scoring weights is not stated in the code, so treat the scores as a summary, not a verdict.

sections.name: FacilityHypothesis
sections.title: Facility type guess
sections.what: Holds the guessed facility type, its score and confidence, and the next-best guess with its score.
sections.why: Lets the viewer see the app's best guess about the facility and what else it considered.
sections.watch_out: This is a guess, not a verified fact, and the limitations list should be read with it.

sections.name: ReviewQueueItem
sections.title: Item waiting for human review
sections.what: Describes one flagged issue, with a message, a confidence number and the evidence behind it.
sections.why: Lets a person check uncertain results.
sections.watch_out: The kind is free text, so it is not checked against a fixed list.

sections.name: AccuracyDimension
sections.title: One accuracy measure
sections.what: Holds a count of passed checks out of the total checks, plus the limitations of that measure.
sections.why: Lets the viewer see how many checks passed for one area.
sections.watch_out: A total of zero would make the share undefined, so code dividing these must guard against it.

sections.name: AccuracyReport
sections.title: Four accuracy measures together
sections.what: Groups four accuracy measures: parsing, classification, location and timing.
sections.why: Gives one summary of the model's reliability.
sections.watch_out: None visible in this declaration.

sections.name: ProjectModel
sections.title: Full project data
sections.what: Describes the complete project the app loads, including its components, timeline, structures, review items, evidence and optional extras.
sections.why: This is the main record passed to the screens.
sections.watch_out: Many fields are optional, and older saved projects may lack the newer ones, so code must not assume they exist.

sections.name: ProjectReference
sections.title: Summary of a project in an import
sections.what: Describes one project as reported after an import, with activity counts by date set and its dates.
sections.why: Lets the import report list the projects it found.
sections.watch_out: These are counts only; the full detail is in the project model.

sections.name: IngestionWarning
sections.title: One warning from an import
sections.what: Describes one problem found while reading the source, with its code, message, severity, table and row.
sections.why: Lets the import report explain what went wrong or looked odd.
sections.watch_out: The detail values can be text, numbers, true or false, or nothing, so display must handle all of them.

sections.name: IngestionReport
sections.title: Summary of an import
sections.what: Describes what the import read, found and warned about, including the column mapping and whether it was cancelled.
sections.why: Lets the viewer see what was imported and what might be missing.
sections.watch_out: A cancelled flag means the import is incomplete, so the results may be partial.

sections.name: JobState
sections.title: Status of a background job
sections.what: Describes the current state of a background import or model job, including its progress numbers, messages, and which projects it covers. It also adds a few app-wide fields to the browser window: a preloaded model, an offline flag, and an accessibility checker.
sections.why: Lets the screen show live progress while the server works.
sections.watch_out: The status is free text that the code compares against words, so a misspelt status is never matched. The window fields are set outside this file.

sections.name: AssemblyTemplate
sections.title: Reusable assembly template
sections.what: Describes a named set of assembly parts that can be reused across components.
sections.why: Lets one template describe many similar components.
sections.watch_out: None visible in this declaration.

summary: Declares the shape of every data record the app reads from the local server or keeps on screen, such as projects, components, activities, evidence, warnings and job status.
purpose: Gives the code a shared contract, so that a missing or misnamed field is caught while the code is being written, not at run time.
why: The app receives large data files from a server, and these shapes describe what to expect. Likely reason: the app is written in TypeScript, which relies on such declarations.
how: Each exported name describes one kind of record. Records refer to each other, for example a project model holds components and components hold schedules. The file also adds a few app-wide fields to the browser window object.
inputs: Nothing is run here. The file is read by the type checker and by other source files.
outputs: No values. The output is type checking: the build fails if a file uses a field that the declaration does not allow.
risks: A declaration can be wrong without any error, because the real data comes from the server. Many fields are optional, so code must check them. Old saved files may lack newer fields.
debug: If a value is undefined or a build error mentions a field, compare the field with the matching declaration here, then check what the server sends.
